First Light · Mobile design brief · version 1

One simple phone app for every role, built on the company's own brand

Date: 22 November 2026. This brief sets the wireframe type, sizes, type, colour and screen layouts. The company brand is used for this first build (logo, palette, phone numbers). Other companies will get their own brand later.

1 · Decisions

What the screens will be

  • Phone first. Every role uses a phone. The layout is designed at 360 to 430 px wide. Wider screens (laptops, tablets) keep the same single column, centred, never wider than 430 px.
  • Bottom tab bar, attached to the bottom edge. Four main items plus "More". Always visible, like WhatsApp, Instagram and YouTube. Thumbs reach it without stretching.
  • Fixed top bar. Shows the screen title, and the logo on home screens. It stays put while the content scrolls.
  • One column of content. Cards and list rows, read top to bottom. No side-by-side panels on a phone.
  • One primary action per screen. It sits in a bottom action area above the tab bar when the screen needs one.
  • Simple illustrations, real numbers. Illustration only for empty states and onboarding. Numbers and status are plain, large and labelled with words.
2 · Wireframe type

Why this structure

The app uses the same structure people already know from WhatsApp, Instagram and YouTube. The three things we copy are the principles, not the designs:

From WhatsApp

Lists with one clear row per item, a status line under each name, and a fixed bottom bar. Nothing is hidden behind a menu.

From Instagram

Cards with a clear image or number first, then the detail. Actions are large and sit where the thumb rests.

From YouTube

A home screen of sections that scroll down. Each section has a title and a "see all" link in the same place.

Our additions

Traffic-light status with a word, stage timers, and a payments area that never shows an amount without its due date.

3 · Sizes and spacing

Rules for every screen

ItemRule
Design width360 to 430 px. Layout uses fluid widths, never a fixed width that can overflow.
Side margin16 px on both sides. No content touches the edge.
Top bar56 px tall. Title at 18 px, with ellipsis if long. Nothing wraps into two lines.
Bottom tab bar72 px including the phone's home-indicator area. Items at least 48 px tall.
Touch targetsAt least 48 px tall and wide. Buttons span the full width on phones.
Body text16 px, line height 1.55. Nothing smaller than 14 px, and 14 px only for secondary labels.
Big numbers24 to 30 px, bold, tabular figures so columns align.
Card spacing14 px between cards, 16 px inside cards. Corners 16 px; buttons 12 px.
OverflowLong names cut with an ellipsis; long lists scroll inside their own area. No horizontal scrolling on any screen.
MotionOnly simple fades and slides, under 250 ms. Respect the phone's reduce-motion setting.
4 · Typography

Fonts

Headings and titles

Playfair Display, semibold. Used for screen headings and section titles only, at 21 px and above. Matches the brochure's headings.

Text, labels and numbers

Poppins, regular, medium and semibold. Clear at 14 px and 16 px on small phones. Numbers use tabular figures. Matches the brochure's body text.

Poppins 400 for body, 500 for labels, 600 for buttons and titles, 700 for big numbers. No other weights.

Avoid: serif text under 21 px, light weights (300 or below), and text set in colour alone to show status.

5 · Colour

Palette from the brochure

Colours sampled from the company's brochure and logo. The contrast ratios were calculated for each pair we use.

Ink#3A3158 · main text, dark cards, primary buttons · 11.9:1 on white
Cream#F6F2E8 · screen background · 10.7:1 with ink
White#FFFFFF · cards and bars
Lavender#D8CBEE · section tints, selected tab · 7.8:1 with ink
Blush#F6B1BC · progress and highlights · 6.8:1 with ink
Coral to magentaFrom the logo only · fills, never text
Deep magenta (text accent)#A8246E · small accent text · 6.7:1 on white
Status: on track#1F7A4D text on #E3F2EA · 5.3:1
Status: past target#8A5A00 text on #FBF0D6 · amber, with a word
Status: needs action#B42331 text on #F9E3E5 · 6.5:1
Contrast rule: coral and magenta are too light for text on white (2.3 to 2.6:1). Use them for fills and the logo only. Any text in those colours uses ink or deep magenta.

8 · Responsive behaviour

How the screens adjust

  • Phones 320 to 430 px: single column. Tiles in pairs stay pairs; long names truncate with an ellipsis.
  • Tablets and laptops: the same column, centred, up to 430 px wide. Side space is cream background, not stretched content.
  • Text size: uses the phone's own text-size setting. Layouts use flexible heights, so bigger text grows the card instead of cutting it off.
  • Long content: only the middle area scrolls. The top bar and tab bar stay fixed.
  • Keyboard open: the bottom action area moves above the keyboard. Inputs stay visible.
  • Safe areas: the tab bar and action area respect the phone's bottom inset, so nothing sits under the home indicator.
9 · Reference images

What each reference contributed

Every image you sent is kept here for the team. The app takes principles from them. It does not copy any one design, and it avoids the generic AI look: heavy gradients, glass effects, emoji icons, many floating cards, and decorative 3D.

Dashboard references (4)

Large hero number, a soft card for the score, and small charts. We kept the hero and the gauge idea. We dropped the stacked tiles and the decorative characters.

Pastel and mood images (14)

Used for mood only: calm blush, lavender and cream. They guide the palette and the empty-state illustrations. None appear on working screens.

Logo and brochure (2)

The logo is used in the top bar. The brochure gives the palette, the heading and body fonts, and the number-led contact block.

Typography and palette boards (2)

Confirmed the serif-for-headings, sans-for-text pairing. Used the palette rule of one main colour, one accent and neutral backgrounds.

10 · Before build

Items to confirm

  1. Company name spelling. The logo reads "HOMESIC" and the brochure reads "HOMSIC". This brief uses the brochure spelling. Please confirm the official name before the logo and app name are final.
  2. Contact numbers, email and website. Used as given in the brochure: +91 85270 25058, +91 82104 54320, care@homsic.com, homsic.com. The address is not used on screens until confirmed.
  3. Commercial promises in the brochure. "Delivery in under 30 days" and "₹1,000 per day if delayed" are commercial terms. The app must not show them as rules until the owner confirms them, and the software must track them only if they are part of the agreement.
  4. Font licences. Playfair Display and Poppins are free to use. Confirm that the brochure's fonts are these two; the match is close but not checked against the original files.
